_doc: T-0816. Cohort 14 was read twice by two runs that could not see each other, and the two ledgers disagreed on 36 of the 76 people. This file rules every one of the 36, person by person, with the discriminator that decided it, and pass_14_findings.json — the ledger of record — now carries the ruled outcome and the same discriminator on each person's row. Nothing here mints, promotes or regrades a resident: the rulings are research outcomes, and T-0513/T-0514/T-0515 remain the passes entitled to spend them.

the_ladder._doc: The two passes were not applying two rules so much as two halves of one. The record's rule named the CONTEMPORARY sources by name and treated any partial agreement as a candidate; the rival's rule got the two axes right in words — strength of the name agreement, and the date of the source — and then applied `corroborated` to initial-only agreements in volumes printed fifty years later. The ladder below is the rival's two axes with the record's strictness, and it is what every ruling in this file is decided by.
the_ladder.axis_1_strength: FULL — every name element the resident carries is present in the entry and none conflicts; an initial the source expands counts as FULL only where the residents layer holds exactly one bearer of the surname. PARTIAL — initial-for-initial only, or an expansion two or more men answer to. SURNAME-ONLY — a refusal, always, and this repository's crosswalks already say so in as many words.
the_ladder.axis_2_date: CONTEMPORARY — written at or before the scene year of 1835 and independent of the post-office return. LATER — printed after 1835, however good the entry.
the_ladder.R2_corroborated: FULL agreement in a CONTEMPORARY source.
the_ladder.R1_corroborated_enrichment: FULL agreement in a LATER volume: it enriches the biography and adds no 1835 attestation.
the_ladder.R3_candidate_identity: A NAMED external entry or person in PARTIAL agreement, or in full agreement with no date, place, occupation or kinship discriminator bridging it to the 1835 person. Retained unasserted.
the_ladder.R4_no_corroboration: No named external entry at all beyond the post-office return — an index that only counts cards under a surname, a conflicting element, or refusals only. A documented negative search, not evidence of absence.

salvage_fergus_26_29._doc: Ask 2 of T-0816: the rival branch also carried a directed reading of Fergus's Historical Series 26-29 — the 1843 directory, its advertising pages, its fire-department and civic rolls, and Wentworth's obituary lists — against all 76 cohort names, which the directory claim ledgers do not cover. It is quotation, not opinion, and it would have been lost when the branch is pruned. Every row the reading touched is preserved verbatim here, with the outcome the rival drew from it; the outcome is the rival's, not this project's, and where the two disagree the ruling above governs.

what_stops_this_recurring._doc: Ask 3. Two runs read the same 76 people because nothing they could both see said the cohort was taken. `tools/ticket.mjs inflight` is that signal and it has a COLD WINDOW: a branch is only reported as in flight if it was pushed within the last three hours, so a run that claims, pushes, and then reads for four hours becomes invisible to the very next run at the exact moment it is most expensive to duplicate. The rerun filed this defect itself, and the filing died with the branch.
what_stops_this_recurring.in_the_meantime: A ticket's own state is the durable half of the lock and it does not go cold: `claim` refuses a ticket another branch is on, and `list --workable` keeps a `claimed` ticket in its place. Read both before starting, not one.
